findings.evidence: Lines 365-370: `rw [gammaMatrix_nMinus_mul_goodProjector, …, mul_sub, mul_add, mul_add, mul_smul_comm, mul_smul_comm, …, mul_smul_comm, mul_one, add_mul, smul_mul_assoc, one_mul]` then `module`; lines 328-330 and 340-343 show the same positional `mul_assoc`/`neg_mul`/`mul_neg`/`neg_neg` juggling.
findings.fix: Replace the generic ring steps by an order-independent `simp only [...]` (keeping the content-bearing lemmas, e.g. `gammaMatrix_nMinus_mul_self`, `gammaMatrix_nMinus_mul_gammaMatrix_nPlus`, `gamma5_mul_gammaMatrix`, as explicit rewrites) before the closing `module`/`abel`; for the commutation lemmas, state the one content step as a `have` (`γ⁺ /p = 2p⁺P₋ - /p_T γ⁺`) and conclude from it.
findings.issue: `gammaMatrix_nMinus_mul_gammaMatrix_sub_smul_one` is a 17-entry `rw` chain in which the generic steps (`mul_sub`, `mul_add` twice, `mul_smul_comm` twice, `add_mul`, `smul_mul_assoc`, `mul_one`, `one_mul`, `add_zero`, `smul_zero`) only fire because of rewrite order and first-occurrence matching, so the reason the identity holds is invisible and the proof breaks on any change to the normal form. The same shape occurs at lines 327 (`commute_goodProjector_gamma5`, 12 entries, with positional `← mul_assoc gamma5` / `mul_assoc (gammaMatrix L.nPlus) gamma5`), 340 (`commute_goodProjector_gammaMatrix_of_mem_transverse`, 11), 191 (`goodProjector_mul_badProjector`, 9, with positional `mul_assoc (gammaMatrix L.nPlus)` / `← mul_assoc (gammaMatrix L.nMinus)`), 170 (`goodProjector_add_badProjector`) and 429 (`haT`).

findings.evidence: `grep -n toBilinForm` in the new file: lines 94, 106, 114 use `← ContinuousLinearMap.toBilinForm_apply`; line 480 uses `simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.toBilinForm_apply] at this`. No such lemma exists in the repo: `EpsilonEridani/Relativity/LightConeBasis.lean` only has `minkowskiAxis_plus_apply`/`minkowskiAxis_minus_apply` for the standard basis.
findings.fix: Add three `@[simp]` lemmas for `L : LightConeBasis (minkowskiProduct (d := 3)).toBilinForm` — `⟪L.nPlus, L.nPlus⟫ₘ = 0`, `⟪L.nPlus, L.nMinus⟫ₘ = 1`, `t ∈ L.transverse → ⟪L.nPlus, t⟫ₘ = 0` (plus the `nMinus` duals via `swap`) — and use them at all four sites; the remaining §0.1 material will need them too.
findings.issue: The conversion between Physlib's `⟪·,·⟫ₘ` and the `LightConeBasis` fields is re-done inline four times via `← ContinuousLinearMap.toBilinForm_apply` (lines 94, 106, 114 and, in the other direction, 480), repeated bridging reasoning that is not available to any later proof and that hard-codes a coercion rewrite direction.

findings.evidence: Lines 183-185 define `goodProjector_apply_add_badProjector_apply : L.goodProjector ψ + L.badProjector ψ = ψ`, which with `hbad : L.badProjector ψ = 0` gives the goal directly.
findings.fix: Use the lemma proved at line 183: `simpa [hbad] using L.goodProjector_apply_add_badProjector_apply ψ` (or `have := L.goodProjector_apply_add_badProjector_apply ψ; rwa [hbad, add_zero] at this`).
findings.issue: In `ker_gammaMatrix_nPlus` the forward direction reconstructs `ψ` by rewriting backwards into `add_zero`: `rw [← add_zero (L.goodProjector ψ), ← hbad, ← LinearMap.add_apply, goodProjector_add_badProjector, Module.End.one_apply]`. Backwards `rw` with an explicit argument to create a `+ 0` is brittle and hides that the step is just the already-proved decomposition.

summary: The duality-by-`swap` lemmas are robust and well factored, but the core Clifford-algebra computations are written as long positional `rw` chains over generic ring lemmas (`mul_add`, `mul_smul_comm`, `mul_assoc f`), and the bridge from `minkowskiProduct` to the light-cone-basis fields is re-derived inline at four sites instead of being a lemma.
